items.claim: The adjuration quote, the byte-identity claim made against the earlier full-form site, and the tier-3 parashah disclosure all verify on the pointed bytes.
items.evidence: Re-collated: הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ is byte tier at oshb:Song.3.5 and byte tier at oshb:Song.2.7. The row's stronger claim holds literally, not approximately: oshb:Song.2.7 and oshb:Song.3.5 are byte-identical whole-verse (160 codepoints each, zero divergence at byte, accent-stripped and skeleton tiers), so 'verbatim (tier: byte)' is exact. Shape discipline is intact: this is the full form carrying the gazelles/does and אִם תָּעִ֧ירוּ (byte, oshb:Song.3.5), held apart from the אִֽם תִּמְצְאוּ֙ shape at oshb:Song.5.8 and from the mah-ta'iru shape at oshb:Song.8.4 - four adjuration sites, no harmonized form. The one rival the row leaves untested - folding the verse into the seek-find narration it closes - is nonetheless answered by the bytes: the she-ahavah-nafshi relative formula runs MT 3:1-3:4 and stops at the seam (5 verses book-wide with MT 1:7), while this verse is a verbatim whole-verse repetition of an earlier bracket, which is the byte difference that warrants isolating it here and folding the unique variant at MT 5:8 into its own episode elsewhere in this cluster. The root echo across the 3:4|3:5 seam - שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י (byte, oshb:Song.3.4) against הָאַהֲבָ֖ה (byte, oshb:Song.3.5) - is not a device straddle, since the relative verb formula and the ahavah noun are split objects (5 verses versus 10 verses), so nothing cross-seam is left undisclosed. The setumah at MT 3:5 is disclosed as single-witness tier-3 corroboration and explicitly not the driver; no K/Q verse is touched (the four notes stand at MT 1:17, 2:11, 2:13, 4:9), and no divine-name, special-letter or paseq-position claim is made.
tier_citations: skeleton (she-ahavah-nafshi formula: 5 verses; ahavah noun: 10 verses - split objects)

items.claim: The front-seam driver carries a digit attached to a blended object - the ascending-question formula the row itself quotes is byte-attested in 2 verses, not 3 - and the daughters-of-Jerusalem string it treats as belonging only elsewhere stands inside the span at MT 3:10.
items.evidence: The row's own quoted run מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר re-collates byte at oshb:Song.3.6 and byte at oshb:Song.8.5, but collates 'none' against oshb:Song.6.10, whose question is the ha-nishqafah shape with no ascent clause at all. Contiguous consonantal sweeps separate the objects cleanly: the mi-zot interrogative = 3 verses (skeleton tier: MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5); the ola-min-ha-midbar ascent clause = 2 verses (skeleton tier: MT 3:6, 8:5); the full quoted run = 2 verses at byte tier (MT 3:6, 8:5). The prose names the object as the ascending-question formula and then hangs the 3-verse digit and 'two further sites' on it, which is the blended count the name-the-object-then-count rule bars; the shared staging spine's own label for this set is equally loose, which is precisely the re-derivation the row owed, so the cure is a re-cut object name plus the honest 2-verse byte digit, not a new sweep. Second defect: מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם stands at oshb:Song.3.10, one verse inside the span and one verse before the closing vocative, so the contrast drawn against 'the daughters-of-Jerusalem pair used elsewhere' passes over an in-span occurrence whose address-vs-from-phrase role split is exactly the live hazard here. The Zion digit itself verifies: בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (byte, oshb:Song.3.11) is the only site (1 verse, skeleton tier), and the setumah marks at MT 3:5, 3:8 and 3:11 are disclosed as single-witness tier-3 without being made drivers.
tier_citations: byte (oshb:Song.3.6; same run byte at oshb:Song.8.5)

items.claim: The opener carrying the front seam is an unswept, untiered recurrence claim whose formula stands equally at MT 1:15, the byte-identical refrain interrupting the unit at MT 4:6 is never engaged, and the rival test rests on an imperative the Hebrew of MT 4:8 does not carry.
items.evidence: הִנָּ֨ךְ יָפָ֤ה רַעְיָתִי֙ collates byte at oshb:Song.4.1, but the same formula stands at oshb:Song.1.15 as הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י - accent-stripped tier against the row's quoted run, skeleton-tier identical - so the hinnakh-yafah-rayati opener is a 2-verse formula whose other site opens no wasf; the row cites it with no sweep digit and no tier label while it carries the 3:11|4:1 seam. Inside the claimed unit, עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֨וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים collates byte at oshb:Song.4.6 and byte against oshb:Song.2.17: a book-level refrain (2 verses) sits between the body-part chain, which the row itself stops at web:Song.4.5, and the closural line at 4:7, and the first-person clause following it carries no 2fs marker - the rival division at 4:5|4:6 is neither disclosed nor tested, though it is the granularity question this span actually poses. Third, the rejected alternative turns on 'Song.4.8's imperative come': the form standing there is תָּב֑וֹאִי (byte, oshb:Song.4.8), a 2fs prefix-conjugation, and no imperative form occurs in that verse - the label is imported from the WEB rendering “Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon.” (web:Song.4.8). With no morphology layer staged the claim must stand on the pointed bytes plus both renderings, and the bytes do not supply it. The inclusio the row argues does verify independently: both quoted runs are byte tier at their cited refs and rayati sits at MT 4:1 and MT 4:7 inside a 9-verse book-wide set.
tier_citations: accent_stripped (4:1 run vs oshb:Song.1.15); skeleton (hinnakh-yafah-rayati: 2 verses)

items.claim: The span-wide 'no addressee or gender-marked interruption' is carried by absence over the unit's last two verses and ships without a digit-bearing sweep, and the garden catchword crossing the row's own back seam is undisclosed.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs re-collate byte at their cited refs and the address digits are exact: kallah = 6 verses word-bound (MT 4:8-4:12 and 5:1) with MT 4:8 its first site, and the achoti bride-epithet form = 5 verses (MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12, 5:1, 5:2) once the MT 8:8 sister is role-split off. The universal overstates what the bytes carry, though: the 2fs address chain is attested continuously only through שְׁלָחַ֨יִךְ֙ (byte, oshb:Song.4.13); MT 4:14 and MT 4:15 carry no 2fs suffix and no vocative at all (“a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.” at web:Song.4.15), so the back seam rests on a missing marker rather than on one. Across that same seam the garden lexeme continues at consonantal-stem tier: מַעְיַ֣ן גַּנִּ֔ים (byte, oshb:Song.4.15) then הָפִ֥יחִי גַנִּ֖י (byte, oshb:Song.4.16), inside a word-bound gan-family set of 7 verses (MT 4:12, 4:15, 4:16, 5:1, 6:2, 6:11, 8:13; the ha-magen of MT 4:4 and the aggan of MT 7:3 = WEB 7:2 are contained-substring false hits, not gan-family) - a straddling link the row does not disclose, with its own in-span anchor at גַּ֥ן נָע֖וּל (byte, oshb:Song.4.12). The K/Q-bearing MT 4:9 is correctly disclosed with no K/Q claim made, and the setumah at MT 4:11 is carried as interior tier-3 corroboration only.
tier_citations: skeleton, word-bound (gan-family: 7 verses; kallah: 6 verses; achoti bride-epithet: 5 verses)
tier-3 parashah, single-witness (setumah, MT 4:7 and MT 4:11)

items.claim: The possessor-shift argument is byte-false as stated: no 1cs 'my garden' form occurs anywhere in MT 4:8-4:15, and the only one at this seam stands inside 4:16 itself, in the woman's own address to the winds.
items.evidence: A word-bound gan-family sweep puts the preceding unit's garden tokens at גַּ֥ן נָע֖וּל (byte, oshb:Song.4.12, bare form) and מַעְיַ֣ן גַּנִּ֔ים (byte, oshb:Song.4.15, plural) - neither 1cs-suffixed. The 1cs form first appears in the row's own verse as הָפִ֥יחִי גַנִּ֖י (byte, oshb:Song.4.16), the woman's imperative to the north wind, and next in the man's speech at בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1). Both witnesses agree: “My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.” (web:Song.4.12), “a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.” (web:Song.4.15), and “Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out.” (web:Song.4.16). The shift actually attested therefore runs her 'my garden' to 'his garden' inside one verse, not from a male 'my garden' in 4:8-4:15 handed across the seam, and the 'my garden' half of the row's argument is carried with no quoted form at all, which the engagement standard does not allow for a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim. The seam itself survives on the row's other evidence: יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל collates byte at oshb:Song.4.16 and dodi-exact is a 24-verse set, her word for him, distinct from the 28-verse dod-family and from the defective dodayik standing twice inside MT 4:10 in the man's mouth - five objects the row does not blend but also never names.
tier_citations: dodi-exact 24 verses / dod-family 28 verses / defective dodayik MT 4:10 (object-split)

items.claim: The cross-part continuity the row asserts is left with no byte anchor while two byte-true chains straddle its front seam undisclosed, and the widened-address point leans on the WEB rendering of a dod-family plural the row never names.
items.evidence: The rationale says the verse closes a movement opened before the part's own span but names no verse and quotes no form for it, and the front-seam neighbour is absent from the evidence refs. The byte evidence for that continuity is יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל (byte, oshb:Song.4.16) answered clause-for-clause by בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) with its eat-verb echo, and אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), which continues the man's address vocabulary attested at MT 4:9, 4:10 and 4:12 (achoti bride-epithet: 5 verses; kallah: 6 verses) - neither chain is disclosed, and an undisclosed byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against it. The verse-final דּוֹדִֽים (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) is a dod-family plural, a different object from the 1cs dodi of the surrounding verses and the form the closing 'beloved' of “Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.” (web:Song.5.1, verbatim-verified) renders; the row hangs its widened-address reading on that English line rather than on the form. Its own אִכְל֣וּ רֵעִ֔ים (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) does carry the plural summons independently of any rendering, the setumah at MT 5:1 is correctly tiered single-witness, and the tier-4 speaker apparatus is explicitly refused.
tier_citations: skeleton, word-bound (achoti bride-epithet: 5 verses; kallah: 6 verses)

items.claim: Both of the row's seams carry undisclosed byte-true straddles - the man's address vocabulary continues into MT 5:2 and the daughters quote the oath back at MT 5:9 - while the opening voice claim is carried by the English rather than by the gender-marked Hebrew.
items.evidence: Front seam: אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ stands byte at oshb:Song.5.2 inside the quoted knocking-speech, continuing the achoti chain of MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12 and 5:1 (bride-epithet form: 5 verses) and adding rayati (9 verses book-wide), while ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֣י (byte, oshb:Song.5.2) is one of the 2 qol-dodi sites and would have supported the opening. The role split that resolves this - embedded quotation inside her narration versus continued address - is neither performed nor disclosed, so the front-seam case rests on a tier-3 setumah plus “I was asleep, but my heart was awake.” (web:Song.5.2, verbatim-verified), while the form that actually marks the voice, אֲנִ֥י יְשֵׁנָ֖ה (byte, oshb:Song.5.2, feminine singular), is never quoted and the English carries no gender at all. Back seam: שֶׁכָּ֖כָה הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (byte, oshb:Song.5.9) repeats the oath root immediately across the row's own closing seam, the daughters quoting it back - undisclosed, and it is precisely the same-root site the four-site adjuration count excludes on speech-role grounds, so the disclosure was owed by the row's own shape discipline. That discipline is otherwise exact: both adjuration quotes collate byte at oshb:Song.5.8 and the im-timtze'u/mah-tagidu shape is correctly held apart from the full daughters-plus-gazelles form and from the mah-ta'iru variant, with no harmonized shape anywhere.
tier_citations: skeleton, word-bound (achoti bride-epithet: 5 verses; rayati: 9 verses; qol-dodi: 2 verses)
